summary: Trinidad and Tobago lets citizens of the 42 countries and territories on the Immigration Division’s no-visa list (among them the UK, Canada and most Commonwealth countries) enter without a visa, EU citizens (except Ireland) for up to 90 days in any 180 under the EU waiver agreement, and South Koreans for 90 days under a bilateral agreement; CARICOM nationals get six months under Caribbean free movement. US, Japanese, Brazilian, Irish, Turkish, Serbian and Colombian citizens are visa-free on their own governments’ official word, though the no-visa list does not name them. Nationals of the other countries whose passports the Immigration Division’s eVisa portal accepts — it is open only to nationals of countries requiring a visa — must obtain a visa before traveling, online through that portal, which replaced all earlier visa procedures in April 2024. For the remaining passports, among them most Latin American ones and those of India, Russia, Israel, Norway and Switzerland, no official page we could read states the rule.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Trinidad and Tobago?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. Citizens of the 42 countries and territories on the Immigration Division’s no-visa list — including the UK, Canada and most Commonwealth countries — need no visa, and neither do EU citizens (Ireland is outside the agreement), who get up to 90 days in any 180 under the EU waiver agreement, or South Koreans, who get 90 days under a bilateral agreement. US, Japanese, Brazilian, Irish, Turkish, Serbian and Colombian citizens are visa-free according to their own governments (and, for Brazil, Trinidad and Tobago’s embassy), although the no-visa list does not name them. CARICOM nationals enter under Caribbean free movement with up to six months. Nationals whose passports the Immigration Division’s eVisa portal accepts — it is open only to nationals of countries requiring a visa, and accepts among others Australian, Chinese and Venezuelan nationals — must obtain a visa before traveling, online through that portal, which replaced all earlier visa procedures in April 2024. For the remaining passports, among them most Latin American ones and those of India, Russia, Israel, Norway and Switzerland, no official page we could read states the rule.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Trinidad and Tobago without a visa?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. EU citizens may stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period under the EU waiver agreement and South Koreans up to 90 days under a bilateral agreement; the British, Canadian, US and Japanese governments and Trinidad and Tobago’s embassy in Brazil also give 90 days, and Türkiye and Serbia 30. The Immigration Division’s no-visa list states no length of stay. The UK Foreign Office says a 90-day visit can be extended by applying to the passport and immigration department.

faq.question: What applies to CARICOM citizens?
faq.answer: Trinidad and Tobago's Ministry of Foreign and CARICOM Affairs says a CARICOM national seeking to enter Trinidad and Tobago is granted a definite entry of six months, subject to all immigration requirements. Nationals of the participating CSME states (Antigua and Barbuda, Barbados, Belize, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Jamaica, St Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, St Vincent and the Grenadines and Suriname) who hold a CARICOM Skills Certificate may work without a work permit, and must have a certificate issued elsewhere verified within six months of entry.

faq.question: Can Venezuelan citizens travel to Trinidad and Tobago visa-free?
faq.answer: No. Venezuela is not on the Immigration Division's list of countries whose citizens do not need a visa, and the Immigration Division's eVisa portal accepts Venezuelan nationality: obtain the visa online before travelling.

faq.question: Do I need anything special to attend Carnival?
faq.answer: No official source we could read describes a separate permit or visa for Carnival; visitors enter under the normal rules for their passport. The UK government's travel advice warns that robberies and opportunistic crime may occur during the Carnival period.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination?
faq.answer: Not for entry: Trinidad and Tobago reports no yellow fever certificate requirement to WHO, whichever country you arrive from. Vaccination is recommended from 9 months of age if you are going to the densely forested areas of Trinidad, but not for trips limited to Tobago.
